newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares soar 4.66 pct after cabinet meeting.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares soar 4.66 pct after cabinet meeting.

text.p: Istanbul shares surged in late buying on Thursday after the Islamist-led government agreed at a cabinet meeting to implement measures to combat Islamist activism in line with the decisions of the secularist military.
The IMKB National-100 closed 67 points, or 4.66 percent higher at 1,504, following a 2.3 percent morning rise fuelled by positive expectations ahead of the meeting.
Trade volume jumped to 25.50 trillion lira ($204.5 million) from 20.07 trillion ($160.5 million) on Wednesday.
"There was an overall buying activity on positive news about the cabinet meeting," said Serdar Karatepe from Polen securities.
Brokers expect the index to continue its upward move on Friday, with the index testing an initial barrier of 1,550.
A government spokesman said the coalition was committed to enforcing a crackdown on religious activism demanded by the secularist military.

Tension had mounted early last week due to a row between the Islamists and the army following a February 28 National Security Council (MGK) statement urging action against rising Islamist zeal. The statement was later signed by PM Erbakan.
